back: Due to an oversight in the C++ specification, modern compilers typically treat std::int8_t and std::uint8_t the same as signed char and unsigned char respectively. Thus on most modern systems, the 8-bit fixed-width integral types will behave like char types.
front: What is unique about std::int8_t and std::uint8_t
source_text: the same as signed char and unsigned char respectively. Thus on most modern systems, the 8-bit fixed-width integral types will behave like char types.
